 The 5 New Rules For U.S. Travelers As REAL ID Enforcement Nears

 Justin Fenwick is a travel journalist who specializes in national parks and outdoor travel reporting. He covers the stories that shape how people plan and experience their trips across the United States.
Justin has spent years traveling widely across the United States and abroad, and that firsthand experience informs the way he covers the places he writes about. He is currently in the process of becoming a travel agent. When he is not writing, he can often be found planning his next trip or looking for an excuse to get outdoors.

 Travelers moving through American airports and border crossings are navigating a series of significant regulatory shifts as federal agencies modernize identification and health screening protocols. Between 2025 and 2028, a sequence of new requirements from the Department of State and the Department of Homeland Security is changing how citizens and residents prove their identity.

 While some of these updates are procedural and require no immediate action, others carry strict deadlines that could prevent a traveler from boarding a domestic flight or entering the country. Understanding specific dates and the groups affected by each change is essential for avoiding travel disruptions.
 These updates include new travel requirements for both domestic and international flights that have already begun to reshape the travel landscape.

 Posts 
 1 
 By  
 Stacey Sloughfy 
 REAL ID Full Enforcement Deadline
 TSA officer handling REAL ID to a traveler Credit: Shutterstock 
 The REAL ID Act has reached its final implementation stages after years of delays and extensions. For travelers using domestic air transport, the most significant date on the calendar is now May 5, 2027. This marks the point of full enforcement when every traveler must present a compliant license or another accepted form of federal identification to pass through security checkpoints.
 Federal agencies have already begun a phased approach that started on May 7, 2025 . This allowed for a gradual transition rather than a single, abrupt cutoff for the millions of people who fly within the United States every year.
 How To Know Your REAL ID Is Compliant
 This transition period serves as a buffer for state motor vehicle departments and the public to ensure everyone has the necessary documentation before the 2027 deadline. While many states have issued compliant cards for years, some travelers still carry older versions that will not meet the new standards. It is important to look for the star symbol in the upper right corner of a driver's license to confirm it is REAL ID compliant. Those without a compliant card will need to use a passport or military identification once the deadline arrives.
 Online DS-11 Passport Application Pilot
 Online Passport Application form Credit: Rawpixel.com/Shutterstock 
 The Department of State has launched a significant modernization effort for first-time passport applicants. On November 16, 2026, the agency began a pilot program for an online version of the DS-11 application form . This pilot, which is accessible through the America.gov portal, represents a shift away from the traditional requirement of mailing paper forms or visiting an acceptance facility for every step of the process.
 Currently, the program is specifically targeted at adult applicants who are using naturalization certificates as their primary evidence of U.S. citizenship, providing a more streamlined digital path for this specific group of travelers. This pilot is scheduled to remain active until November 20, 2027, allowing the government to test the infrastructure and security of digital submissions before a potential wider rollout.
 Secretary of State Marco Rubio highlighted the initiative at a recent event, noting that the goal is to reduce processing times and administrative burdens for the public, as reported by state.gov . While the online option is available for certain applicants, many travelers still risk being denied boarding when they fail to check their passport expiration dates against the six-month passport validity rule .
 CDC Air Travel Attestation For DRC
 traveler filling out digital health declaration on smartphone Credit: Boris023/Shutterstock 
 Travelers arriving from the Democratic Republic of the Congo are currently subject to a temporary health attestation requirement. Effective November 3, 2026, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) mandated that all airline passengers who have been in the DRC within the last 21 days must provide specific contact and health information before boarding flights to the United States. This measure is a response to ongoing health concerns in the region and is designed to facilitate rapid contact tracing if a public health risk is identified among arriving passengers.
 How Long The Travel Attestation For DRC Remains Active
 The attestation rule is currently active and is set to remain in effect until December 18, 2026 , unless it is extended or rescinded by health authorities. Airlines are responsible for collecting these attestations before passengers board their flights. Failure to comply can result in boarding denials. This is a highly focused rule that does not affect most international travelers, but for those with recent travel history in Central Africa, it is a mandatory step that must be completed before arrival at a U.S. port of entry.
 Even though it is temporary, the rule carries significant weight for those it affects during its six-week enforcement window.
 Alien Registration And Evidence Rule
 U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS). Credit:  Poetra.RH /Shutterstock 
 A significant update to the regulations surrounding alien registration and evidence of registration took effect earlier this year. On June 29, 2026, the Department of Homeland Security finalized a rule that streamlined the forms and processes used by lawful permanent residents and other noncitizens to maintain their registration status. This change updated Form G-325R and clarified the requirements for carrying evidence of registration. This is a legal obligation for all noncitizens over the age of 18 who remain in the United States for more than 30 days.
 What The Rule Is Designed To Achieve
 The new rule was designed to reduce the administrative burden on both the government and the individuals required to register. It replaced older procedures with a more modern framework that aligns with current digital record-keeping practices. While many travelers may not interact with these forms on a daily basis, the legal requirement to possess valid registration evidence remains a cornerstone of U.S. immigration law.
 This item impacts millions of lawful residents who may need to update their documentation to remain compliant with federal law. It serves as a reminder that travel rules often extend beyond the airport gate and into the long-term status of those living within the country.
 Series B Single Sized Passport Book
 Traveler's hand holding U.S. passport while sitting on an airplane Credit: KieferPix / Shutterstock.com 
 The Department of State has announced a major change to the physical design and options available for U.S. passport books. Starting in 2028, the government will move to a single-sized Series B passport book that contains 38 pages. This marks the end of the current system where applicants can choose between a standard 26-page book and a larger 50-page version for frequent travelers.
 The new 38-page standard is intended to simplify production and provide a uniform document that meets the needs of the vast majority of American citizens. This redesign is part of the Next Generation Passport initiative, which incorporates enhanced security features and a new aesthetic that highlights American history and culture.
 Travelers do not need to replace their current passports immediately, as existing books remain valid until their expiration dates. However, once the 2028 rollout begins, all new and renewed passports will follow the 38-page Series B format. This change follows other recent warnings where the government warns travelers may need more than a passport to fly this summer due to evolving entry rules.
